philosophy.title: Pedagogical Philosophy & Educational Vision
philosophy.summary: Bridging abstract biological concepts with hands-on computational execution. I design courses and workshops that treat command-line proficiency, reproducible version control, and rigorous algorithmic reasoning as core competencies for modern life scientists.

pillars.title: Active, Terminal-First Learning
pillars.description: Every lecture is paired with real-world computational problem sets where students analyze actual sequencing data rather than synthetic toy examples.

pillars.title: Reproducibility as a Core Value
pillars.description: Teaching Git version control, containerized environments (Docker/Singularity), and workflow orchestrators (Nextflow) from day one.

pillars.title: Inclusive Mentorship & Trainee Ownership
pillars.description: Empowering students through transparent authorship compacts, weekly 1-on-1 milestone tracking, and individualized development plans (IDPs).

courses.title: Bioinformatics and Big Data Mining
courses.description: Advanced computational methods for biological big data: high-throughput sequencing analysis, sequence alignment algorithms, structural modeling, machine learning in genomics, and high-performance computing cluster utilization.
topics: NGS Quality Control & Variant Calling Pipelines (GATK, FreeBayes)
Machine Learning Classifiers in Scikit-Learn and PyTorch
Slurm HPC Job Scheduling & Shell Scripting

courses.title: Bioinformatics Tools and Their Application in Agriculture
courses.description: Comprehensive graduate curriculum covering biological databases, molecular phylogenetics, pairwise and multiple sequence alignment, protein secondary structure prediction, and applied crop genomics.
topics: Biological Data Mining & NCBI / Ensembl E-utilities
Molecular Marker Discovery (SSRs and SNPs in Plant Breeding)

courses.title: Advances in Bioinformatics
courses.description: In-depth doctoral seminar on emerging computational frontiers: comparative genomics, transcriptomic differential expression modeling, protein-protein interaction networks, and structural docking algorithms.
topics: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) in Gene Prediction

courses.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics
courses.description: Foundational course establishing core computational competencies for undergraduate biotechnology majors, including Linux shell basics, sequence formats, and web-based analytical servers.
topics: Biological Sequence Formats (FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM, GFF3)
Primer Design & In Silico PCR Diagnostics

courses.title: Introduction to Genomics and Proteomics
courses.description: High-throughput technologies in genomics and proteomics: whole-genome shotgun sequencing, microarrays, mass spectrometry data analysis, and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins.
topics: Mass Spectrometry Peptide Identification & UniProt Proteomes

courses.title: Computational Biology
courses.description: Mathematical models in molecular biology, algorithm design for biological strings, population genetics modeling, and computational scripting.
topics: Introduction to Python Scripting for Biologists

courses.title: In-house Hands-On Computational Training
courses.description: Intensive semester-long capstone internship supervising senior undergraduate researchers on dedicated bioinformatics software development and genomic analysis projects.
topics: Final Capstone Thesis & Oral Defense Preparation

workshops.title: NGS Data Analysis Workshop: From FastQ to Differential Expression
workshops.description: Hands-on immersion covering quality control, splice-aware alignment (STAR), read quantification, differential gene expression (DESeq2), and interactive pathway visualization using pySeqRNA.

workshops.title: Linux Command-Line & HPC Cluster Scripting for Biologists
workshops.description: Designed to transform bench biologists into confident computational practitioners: bash scripting, text manipulation (grep, awk, sed), SSH remote computing, and Slurm workload submission.

workshops.title: Machine Learning in Bioinformatics: Deep Learning & Sequence Models
workshops.description: Introduction to supervised and unsupervised machine learning in genomics: feature encoding (k-mers, one-hot, embeddings), random forests, convolutional neural networks, and protein language model inference.

mentoring.details: Mentor Ph.D. and M.S. graduate students and diagnostic laboratory personnel in computational genomics, Nextflow DSL2 pipelines, viral phylogenetics, and amplicon sequencing workflows for real-time outbreak surveillance.

Mentored undergraduate and master's researchers in machine learning pipeline architecture, deep neural network training, reproducible benchmarking, and web server deployment across kaabil.net and bioinfo.usu.edu.
Supervised more than 30 undergraduate capstone theses and co-advised graduate research projects in plant genomics, molecular marker discovery, and computational software development.
Supervised undergraduate research projects and laboratory internships in biotechnology and sequence analysis, actively fostering STEM retention and research careers for women scientists.
